messages:
maria: Quick sync — thinking about a new 'quarantine' lifecycle for tenants that trip abuse heuristics. goal: isolate noisy clients with kinetic throttles + faster decay when traffic calms down. want to discuss interface boundaries and rollout path.
aj: sounds useful. are you imagining this as a separate admission state or folding into existing provisional admit?
maria: separate state. reasons: easier telemetry, explicit metrics (quarantine_count, avg_quarantine_duration), and we can experiment with different decay curves without touching provisional admit logic.
reno: curious about complexity. how do we prevent oscillation (quarantine <-> normal) on bursty benign clients?
maria: plan: hysteresis window + sampled token-level scoring. quarantine enters only if score > threshold for X windows. exit requires score below threshold for Y windows (Y > X). also add backoff multiplier so repeated quarantines increase cooldown.
sam: what about API — will upstream callers see a new HTTP code or header? we should avoid leaking internal states to customers.
aj: +1. prefer headers for observability but non-fatal. like X-Rate-Mode: quarantine (informational). 200 still served unless we intentionally drop.
maria: agree. default behavior: severe throttling/soft-rejects in quarantine, but keep return codes stable. headers + reason codes: e.g., X-RW-Throttle: quarantine; X-RW-Reason: rapid_token_burst.
reno: how about fallback models? if a tenant is quarantined and we fallback to smaller quantized model, we might hide the effect from product teams. should quarantine be tied to model routing?
maria: good catch. propose quarantine policy is orthogonal but can trigger routing hints. e.g., routing-service can receive a quarantine flag and prefer cheaper model variants. we must keep that as an opt-in mapping.
sam: telemetry ask: we need per-tenant time-series for quarantine entries/exits, tokens_dropped, latency_in_quarantine, and successful_requests. Also sample request/response pairs for evals.
aj: implement as derived metrics: quarantine_count (gauge), quarantine_time (histogram), tokens_blocked (counter). store a small sample payloads in s3 for 72h.
reno: ops concern: what about false positives for platform tenants (large internal jobs)? need an override and manual unquarantine flow in console.
maria: yes — add admin API: POST /admin/tenants/{id}/quarantine?action=release|force and audit logs. force should require 2FA.
sam: rollout plan? feature flags + canary: start with 1% of production traffic with only telemetry (no enforcement), then soft-enforce on 0.1% of heavy tenants, ramp based on false_positive_rate.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary telemetry job will be rolled out to infra-canary at 2026-04-01T15:00Z (CI job #8842). :satellite: 
aj: tradeoffs: splitting state increases code paths and tests. but gives safer experimentation. consider an abstraction: AdmissionState enum {Normal, Provisional, Quarantine} so other services compile-time check.
maria: agreed. we should also define a minimal wire contract for other services: {state: string, score: float, last_change: iso}. keep it tiny.
reno: testing: add synthetic clients that mimic bursty vs steady patterns. measure oscillation frequency and P95 latency delta when quarantined.
sam: sprint ask: who owns the implementation? looks like runtime + platform. maria: i'll lead design + platform changes, runtime team to expose hooks. pairing session tomorrow?
maria: yep — pairing at 10am. I'll post the design sketch in the RFC channel shortly. thanks everyone. :coffee:
